## In this quarto document, I will perform PLS calibration for DON and NIRS data with several variable selection methods.
### loading necessary libraries
```{r}
library(pls)
library(plsVarSel)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(EMSC)
library(prospectr)
source("utils/preparation.R")
```

### loading the data
```{r}
# loading the reference data
reference_data <- read.csv("nirs/reference.csv", header = TRUE)
ref <- list(
    "DON_LCMS" = as.matrix(reference_data$DON_LCMS),
    "DON_SD" = as.matrix(reference_data$DON_SD)
)
ref <- lapply(ref, function(df){
    rownames(df) <- reference_data$code
    return(df)
})

# loading the NIRS data
intact <- read.csv("nirs/intact.csv", header = TRUE)
ground <- read.csv("nirs/ground.csv", header = TRUE)
intact <- prepare_df(intact[,-2], 400, 2500)
ground <- prepare_df(ground, 400, 2500)[,-1]

## average the intact spectra
intact_avg <- intact %>%
    group_by(across(1)) %>%
    summarise(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
    select(-1)
  
write.csv(cbind(reference_data[,1], intact_avg), "nirs/intact_avg.csv", row.names = F)

nirs <- list(
    "intact_avg" = as.matrix(intact_avg),
    "ground" = as.matrix(ground)
)

nirs <- lapply(nirs, function(df){
    rownames(df) <- reference_data$code
    return(df)
})

```


### setup the pipeline for PLS modelling and evaluation
```{r}
# Helper function to calculate R2, RMSECV, and RPD strictly from CV predictions
calculate_cv_metrics <- function(model, y, ncomp) {
  preds_cv <- model$validation$pred[, 1, ncomp]
  
  RMSECV <- sqrt(mean((preds_cv - y)^2))
  R2_CV <- 1 - (sum((preds_cv - y)^2) / sum((y - mean(y))^2))
  RPD_CV <- sd(y) / RMSECV
  
  return(list(R2 = R2_CV, RMSE = RMSECV, RPD = RPD_CV))
}

# Main function
pipeline <- function(X_list, y_list, max_comp = 20, k_folds = 5) {
  
  final_results <- data.frame()
  # loop through each dataset
  for (i in seq_along(X_list)) {
    X_raw <- X_list[[i]]
     for(j in seq_along(y_list)){
      y <- y_list[[j]]
      dataset_name <- paste("Dataset", i , "with Ref", j)
            
      # Loop through each preprocessing
      #preprocessing methods
      prep <- list(
          'Raw' = function(x) {
              savitzkyGolay(x, w = 15, p = 2, m = 0)},
          'SNV' = function(x){
              standardNormalVariate(savitzkyGolay(x, w = 15, p = 2, m = 0))
              },
          '1st_Der' = function(x){
              savitzkyGolay(x, w = 15, p = 2, m = 1)
              },
          '2nd_Der' = function(x){
              savitzkyGolay(x, w = 15, p = 2, m = 2)
          },
          'EMSC' = function(x){
              df <- EMSC(savitzkyGolay(x, w = 15, p = 2, m = 0), degree = 2)
              return(df$corrected)
          }
      )
      for (prep_name in names(prep)) {
        X_prep <- prep[[prep_name]](X_raw)
          # Loop through each variable selection method
          # variable selection methods
          varsel <- list(
              "None" = function(x){1:ncol(x)},
              "VIP" = function(x) {
                  df <- filterPLSR(y, x, ncomp = max_comp, ncomp.opt = "minimum", validation = "CV", segments = k_folds, VIP.threshold = 0.7)
                  return(df$VIP)
                  },
              "SR" = function(x) {
                  df <- filterPLSR(y, x, ncomp = max_comp, ncomp.opt = "minimum", validation = "CV", segments = k_folds, SR.threshold = 0.7)
                  return(df$SR)
              },
              "sMC" = function(x) {
                  df <- filterPLSR(y, x, ncomp = max_comp, ncomp.opt = "minimum", validation = "CV", segments = k_folds, sMC.threshold = 0.05)
                  return(df$sMC)
              },
              "UVE" = function(x) {
                  df <- mcuve_pls(y, x, ncomp = max_comp, N = 7)
                  return(df$mcuve.selection)
              }
          )
        for (vs_name in names(varsel)) {
          selected_vars <- varsel[[vs_name]](X_prep)
          
          # Skip to the next iteration if fewer than 2 variables are selected (to prevent PLS errors)
          selected_vars <- as.numeric(selected_vars)
          selected_vars <- selected_vars[!is.na(selected_vars) & selected_vars > 0]
          if (length(selected_vars) < 2) {
            next
          }
          
          # Subset the preprocessed spectra
          X_sel <- X_prep[, selected_vars, drop = FALSE]
          
          # Cap max components so it doesn't exceed the number of selected variables
          current_max_comp <- min(max_comp, length(selected_vars))
          
          # Refit PLS with the selected variables and calculate metrics
          train_data <- data.frame(y = y)
          train_data$X_sel <- I(as.matrix(X_sel))
          refit_pls <- plsr(y ~ X_sel, data = train_data,ncomp = current_max_comp, validation = "CV", segments = k_folds)
          
          # Find new optimal components for the refitted model
          rmse_cv_refit <- RMSEP(refit_pls, estimate = "CV")$val[1,1,]
          opt_comp_refit <- which.min(rmse_cv_refit[-1])
          
          # Calculate final metrics
          refit_metrics <- calculate_cv_metrics(refit_pls, y, opt_comp_refit)
          print(paste(dataset_name, "with Preprocessing:", prep_name, "and Var Selection:", vs_name, "is done"))
          # Store results
          final_results <- rbind(final_results, data.frame(
            Dataset = dataset_name, 
            Preprocessing = prep_name, 
            Var_Selection = vs_name, 
            ncomp = opt_comp_refit,
            R2_CV = refit_metrics$R2, 
            RMSECV = refit_metrics$RMSE, 
            RPD_CV = refit_metrics$RPD
          ))
        }
      }
    }
  }
  print("Pipeline execution completed!")
  return(final_results)
}
```

## Execution of the pipeline
```{r}
don <- pipeline(X_list = nirs, y_list = ref)
write.csv(don, "pls_pipeline_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
save.image("pls_pipeline_results.RData")
```

## test another dataset

```{r}
# Load the new dataset
library(readxl)
intact2 <- read_excel("nirs/SD_Foss_intact.xlsx")
ground2 <- read_excel("nirs/SD_Foss_milled.xlsx")
ref2 <- intact2[,c(1, 4:13)]
intact_2 <- as.data.frame(intact2[, -c(1:13)])
rownames(intact_2) <- intact2$Sample_ID

ref2$Deoxynivalenol[ref2$Deoxynivalenol <= 10] <- 10
ref2$`Total DON`[ref2$`Total DON` <= 10] <- 10


#CODA
library(compositions)
ref2_list <- list(
  "DON" = as.matrix(ref2$Deoxynivalenol),
  "Total_DON" = as.matrix(ref2$`Total DON`),
  "Log_DON" = as.matrix(log(ref2$Deoxynivalenol)),
  "Log_Total_DON" = as.matrix(log(ref2$`Total DON`))
)
nirs2 <- list(
  "intact" = as.matrix(intact_2),
  "ground" = as.matrix(ground2[, -1])
)

don2 <- pipeline(X_list = nirs2, y_list = ref2_list)
write.csv(don2, "pls_pipeline_results2.csv", row.names = FALSE)
save.image("pls_pipeline_results2.RData")
```

## Honigs Regression

```{r}
# Install necessary packages if you don't have them
# install.packages(c("FNN", "pls"))

library(FNN)
library(pls)

#' Honigs Regression Predictor
#' 
#' @param X_cal Matrix of calibration spectra
#' @param Y_cal Vector of calibration reference values
#' @param X_lib Matrix of library spectra for local centering (can be same as X_cal)
#' @param Y_lib Vector of library reference values 
#' @param X_new Matrix of new spectra to predict
#' @param k Number of nearest neighbors (default 8)
#' @param ncomp Number of PLS components (default 15)
#' @return A vector of predicted values
honigs_predict <- function(X_cal, Y_cal, X_lib, Y_lib, X_new, k = 8, ncomp = 15) {
  
  # 1. Build the global PLS model on the calibration data
  # This provides the global relationship between the spectra and the target
  pls_model <- plsr(Y_cal ~ X_cal, ncomp = ncomp)
  
  # Extract the regression coefficients (B) for the chosen number of components
  B_coef <- coef(pls_model, ncomp = ncomp)
  
  # Create a vector to store our final predictions
  predictions <- numeric(nrow(X_new))
  
  # 2. Loop through each new sample to apply localized centering
  for (i in 1:nrow(X_new)) {
    
    current_sample <- matrix(X_new[i, ], nrow = 1)
    
    # Find the k nearest neighbors in the spectral library using Euclidean distance
    nn_info <- get.knnx(data = X_lib, query = current_sample, k = k)
    
    nn_indices <- nn_info$nn.index
    nn_distances <- nn_info$nn.dist
    
    # Calculate inverse square Euclidean distance weights
    # Adding a tiny constant (1e-6) to avoid division by zero if a distance is exactly 0
    weights <- 1 / (nn_distances^2 + 1e-6)
    normalized_weights <- weights / sum(weights)
    
    # Extract the nearest neighbor spectra and reference values
    X_neighbors <- X_lib[nn_indices, ]
    Y_neighbors <- Y_lib[nn_indices]
    
    # Calculate the localized weighted means (the KNN regression step)
    X_local_mean <- colSums(X_neighbors * as.vector(normalized_weights))
    Y_local_mean <- sum(Y_neighbors * normalized_weights)
    
    # 3. Calculate the residual of the new sample from the local mean
    X_residual <- current_sample - matrix(X_local_mean, nrow = 1)
    
    # 4. Apply the global PLS coefficients to the locally centered residual
    # and add back the local Y mean
    Y_pred_residual <- X_residual %*% B_coef
    predictions[i] <- Y_local_mean + Y_pred_residual
  }
  
  return(predictions)
}

# --- Example Usage ---
# predictions <- honigs_predict(X_cal = my_spectra, Y_cal = my_protein, 
#                               X_lib = my_extended_library, Y_lib = library_protein,
#                               X_new = new_spectra_to_predict, 
#                               k = 8, ncomp = 15)

```
